Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years for rape and sexual assaults
metadata.contentSnippet: Former comedian and actor Russell Brand has been sentenced to more than ten years years after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years for rape and sexual assaults
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Russell Brand has been sentenced to more than ten years, following convictions of rape and sexual assault. The 51-year-old former actor and comedian was found guilty at Southwark Crown Court of raping a woman in 2009 and sexually assaulting three others, all of whom were female TV and radio workers. The offences took place between 2004 and 2009, during the height of Brand’s fame. Today, November 9, at Southwark Court, Mr Justice Bennathan, sentenced Brand to 10 years and six months. Russell Brand with his wife Laura Gallacher (Image: Maja Smiejkowska/PA) On Monday, Mr Justice Bennathan slammed Brand’s “staggering arrogance” as he sentenced him to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and three counts of sexual assault. Sentencing judge Mr Justice Bennathan told rapist comedian Russell Brand he had become a “sexual predator” as he was starting to become famous. Beginning his sentencing remarks, he told the defendant: “About 20 years ago, Russell Brand, you were becoming famous. “You were clever – and in many people’s eyes, funny and charismatic. “You had also become a sexual predator.” Mr Justice Bennathan told the court: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and demand justice in the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Mr Brand, act without their consent.” The judge told Brand “imprisonment will deprive your children of the presence of their father, that sad loss to them however is caused by your serious offending.” The judge said factors in mitigation for Brand included his lack of previous convictions and that “17 years had passed” since his final offence, and how Brand had lived his life subsequently including helping those “wrestling with addictions”. Brand showed no emotion as he was jailed for 10 years and six months, but told his wife “we’ll be OK” as he was taken downstairs by the dock officers. The couple shared a brief conversation before the shamed comedian was taken downstairs. Ahead of the sentencing, victim statements were shared in the courtroom, with Brand's rape victim sharing: "When I eventually reported what had happened, it was not simply because of the media documentary. "By that stage I had become aware of the police investigation and felt that I was finally in a stronger position mentally to disclose my experience. "Reporting what happened was something I had hoped I would eventually be able to do, but it took a long time to reach that point." The sentencing follows a four-week trial that revealed how Brand used his celebrity status to exploit and abuse women. During the trial, Brand described his life as “promiscuous” and "full of idiocy," but claimed all sexual encounters were consensual and denied any criminal wrongdoing. Victims, however, painted a starkly different picture of a powerful man who kissed and groped women moments after meeting them, pursued sexual encounters aggressively, and later dismissed or ridiculed them for objecting to his behaviour. Brand was found guilty of raping a 21-year-old fan in 2009, whom he met after a stand-up show at the Hammersmith Apollo. Russell Brand leaves Southwark Crown Court, London, (Image: PA) The woman, who told jurors she was a huge Brand fan, told jurors she had consensually participated in a threesome with the comedian backstage that night, despite having a boyfriend. She later visited Brand’s Hampstead home for sex, but said the encounter turned violent when he forcibly raped her. Brand was also convicted of sexually assaulting a woman at a Nordic bar in Soho in 2004, groping her breasts just seconds after being introduced to her. Another victim described how Brand kissed and groped her during a 2005 visit to Capital Radio’s London studios, and said she looked to his entourage for help but no one intervened. Brand was also convicted of putting his head into the groin of a female Channel 4 worker, after she had been forced to give him a massage in 2009. The woman told the court how Brand had refused to continue a recording session unless she massaged him, and members of his entourage encouraged it instead of protecting her. During the trial, Brand’s 2007 memoir, My Booky Wook, was cited as evidence, including his claim that he would not stop pursuing sex until achieving his "birthright orgasm." Russell Brand and his wife Laura Gallacher outside Southwark Crown Court. (Image: PA) Brand was cleared of two other rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. Following his convictions, the Metropolitan Police confirmed Brand is under investigation for two additional rape allegations. Sir Mark Rowley, Metropolitan Police Commissioner, warned that more victims may come forward.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A driver has been arrested after a woman died in a five-vehicle crash on a busy road near the Cambridgeshire border. The collision took place on the A605 between Warmington and Elton, near Peterborough, at around 1.30am on Sunday, November 8. The driver of a BMW 2 travelling towards Thrapston was involved in a crash with the driver of a BMW X6 heading in the opposite direction towards Peterborough. Two HGV drivers travelling towards Peterborough stopped at the scene to help, at which point a Kia Ceed collided with the stationary BMW 2. The driver of the BMW X6, a woman in her 40s, sadly died as a result of the injuries she sustained in the collision. The driver of the BMW 2, a man in his 20s, sustained serious injuries and has been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. Both HGV drivers were injured in the collision involving the Kia Ceed and the BMW 2, with one sustaining serious injuries. A passenger in the Kia Ceed suffered minor injuries. The A605 was closed after the crash but has since reopened. Detectives from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit are appealing for witnesses or anyone with dashcam footage of the incident to come forward. Anyone with information is asked to email Northamptonshire Police, call the Drivewatch Hotline on 0800 174615, or contact the force on 101. Callers should quote incident number 26000690175 when providing any information.

metadata.title: Plans go in for up to nine more homes on agricultural land on village outskirts
metadata.contentSnippet: Plans have been submitted for up to nine homes on farmland behind eight approved houses in Warboys.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Plans go in for up to nine more homes on agricultural land on village outskirts
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. Plans have been submitted for up to nine homes on farmland behind eight approved houses in Warboys. The application seeks permission in principle for between six and nine homes on 0.85 hectares north of Heath Road, on the village’s north-eastern edge. If approved, the two schemes could provide up to 17 homes on this stretch of Heath Road. S Robinson submitted the latest proposal, with David Mead of The Planning Partnership as planning agent, and Huntingdonshire District Council granted permission for the eight-home development on October 20. A diagram showing the proposed layout of the development. (Image: HDC) Permission in principle would let the council decide whether the site, its residential use and the scale of development are acceptable. The council would consider the details later if permission is granted. Those matters would include the layout, design, landscaping, drainage and access arrangements. The land is currently used for agriculture. Field drains border the site to the north and east, while an Anglian Water pumping station lies to the west. The approved eight-home scheme is directly to the south. Access would run from Heath Road through the entrance approved for the existing scheme. A road would then run north along the western side of those homes. Planning documents say the site is suitable because it adjoins the approved development and would create a "compact, defined extension" to Warboys. But the supporting statement admits the proposal would create a second row of homes behind the linear development along Heath Road. It also acknowledges that the homes would push the village further into the countryside. The applicants say the impact would be limited because the homes would sit against the approved development and existing features contain the site. Documents say the site is in Flood Zone 1 and has no statutory ecological, landscape or heritage designation. The historic Warboys Sheep Wash, classed as a non-designated heritage asset, is east of Heath Pond. The application also cites the district council’s housing land supply. Documents say the authority has 3.68 years’ worth of deliverable housing sites, below the required five years. They put the shortfall at 1,562 homes. The applicants argue that the benefit of providing more housing would outweigh the limited harm caused by development outside the existing built-up area, extending into the countryside and removing agricultural land. Huntingdonshire District Council will decide whether permission in principle should be granted. Warboys Parish Council had objected to the earlier Heath Road scheme, citing its unsustainable location, harm to the countryside and poor integration with the village.

metadata.title: IN PHOTOS: Hundreds gather in Huntingdon for Remembrance Sunday parade and service
metadata.contentSnippet: Huntingdon honours fallen service personnel at Remembrance Sunday parade on November 8, with Armistice Day service and two-minute silence on November 11.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: IN PHOTOS: Hundreds gather in Huntingdon for Remembrance Sunday parade and service
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Hundreds of residents, veterans, serving personnel, cadets and community organisations gathered in Huntingdon on Sunday November 8 to honour those who have lost their lives in military conflicts, whilst serving their country. The annual Remembrance Sunday Parade and Service, organised by Huntingdon Town Council in partnership with the Royal British Legion Huntingdon Branch and RAF Wyton, saw the RAF Wyton Area Voluntary Band lead the parade of RAF Wyton serving personnel, and local cadet groups from all three armed branches. The parade marched from Princes Street to Huntingdon’s Market Square for a moving Service of Remembrance at the Thinking Soldier War Memorial. Wreaths were laid by a wide range of representatives, including Dr Jaspal Singh DL on behalf of the Lord-Lieutenant of Cambridgeshire, Amanda Norton for the Royal British Legion’s Huntingdon Branch, and the Mayor of Huntingdon, Councillor Patrick Kadewere, together with senior representatives from local authorities, RAF Wyton and RAF Alconbury. Many community groups, charities, cadet organisations and local associations laid wreaths during the ceremony. Following the service, the parade reformed and marched through Huntingdon town centre, with the Mayor of Huntingdon and Deputy Lieutenant receiving the salute from participants as they passed along the High Street. The Mayor of Huntingdon, Councillor Patrick Kadewere, said: "It was wonderful to see so many people come together to pay their respects and reflect on the sacrifices made by generations of servicemen and women. "On behalf of Huntingdon Town Council, I would like to thank everyone who took part in the parade, attended the service, laid a wreath, volunteered, or simply stood in silence with us. "Your presence helps ensure that remembrance remains at the heart of our community." The mayor and Huntingdon Town Council has since thanked all those who contributed to the success of the commemorations. A spokesperson for the council said: "In particular, thanks are extended to Royal Air Force Wyton, The Royal British Legion (Huntingdon Branch), The Military Wives Choir of Wyton and Brampton, the RAF Wyton Area Voluntary Band, and Reverend Jan Smith, Chaplain working with Deaf and Deafblind people in Ely Diocese, ensuring the day was both meaningful and accessible for all those attending." Armistice Day service Huntingdon's commemorations continue with the annual Armistice Day Service at the War Memorial in Market Square on Wednesday November 11. The service will commence at 10:55am, ahead of the National Two-Minute Silence at 11:00am, and will include prayers, readings and wreath laying. All are welcome to attend as the community once again comes together in remembrance.

metadata.title: Ground Force presenter Tommy Walsh dies at the age of 69
metadata.contentSnippet: The broadcaster was best known for fronting the BBC garden makeover show which aired from 1997 to 2005.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Ground Force presenter Tommy Walsh dies at the age of 69
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Ground Force presenter Tommy Walsh has died at the age of 69 following a “long illness”, his agent has confirmed. The broadcaster was best known for fronting the BBC garden makeover show from 1997 to 2005. Walsh’s agent, Debbie Schiesser, told the Press Association: “Tommy died peacefully after a long illness surrounded by his family. As this has only just happened, we would ask everyone to please respect the family’s privacy.” Walsh, from Hackney, London, presented Ground Force alongside Alan Titchmarsh and Charlie Dimmock. At its peak, the series attracted 12 million viewers. Walsh, a builder by trade, later appeared on other home improvement shows including Homes Under The Hammer and Clean It, Fix It. He was also a contestant on weight loss show Celebrity Fit Club, and appeared on Lily Savage’s Blankety Blank and quiz show Pointless. Walsh was previously diagnosed with throat cancer in 2022 after a doctor found a lump during a GP appointment. The presenter made a full recovery. Prior to his television career, Walsh ran his own property business. One of his clients was a TV producer who invited him to a screen test, kickstarting his career in front of the camera. He was married to his wife Marie and was a father to three children: Charlotte, Natalie and Jonjo.

metadata.title: Face of controlling partner who strangled victim amid decade of abuse
metadata.contentSnippet: A controlling partner from Peterborough who subjected his victim to a decade of abuse and even strangled her has been jailed for more than two years.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Face of controlling partner who strangled victim amid decade of abuse
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A controlling partner who subjected his victim to a decade of abuse and even strangled her has been jailed for more than two years. Anthony Bernard, 49, of Croyland Road, Walton, Peterborough, pleaded guilty to engaging in controlling or coercive behaviour in an intimate or family relationship and intentional strangulation. His abuse came to light after an incident on August 11, when he emptied his partner’s wardrobe, took her belongings, and threatened to burn them in a car. Police uncovered more than a decade of coercive and controlling behaviour during their investigation. Bernard had installed cameras around the home to monitor the victim, restricted her contact with friends, and tried to prevent her from having hobbies. He regularly questioned her about her whereabouts, went through her phone while she slept, and checked her smartwatch to track how far she had travelled. If she was out longer than expected, he would accuse her of cheating. When the victim challenged his behaviour, Bernard became aggressive and verbally abusive, often punching walls in anger, leaving her frightened. In June last year, he pinned the victim against a wall and strangled her during an argument. Anthony Bernard admitted engaging in controlling or coercive behaviour (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Bernard was jailed for two years and three months and given a restraining order at Cambridge Crown Court on Wednesday, November 4. Detective Constable Isabelle Wilding said: "Bernard subjected his victim to years of controlling behaviour, monitoring her movements, restricting her contact with friends and invading her privacy. "His behaviour left her frightened and was designed to strip away her independence and control different aspects of her life. "I hope this sentence gives her some reassurance and sends a clear message that coercive and controlling behaviour is domestic abuse and we will take reports seriously." To report concerns or for more advice and support on domestic abuse, including coercive control, visit Cambridgeshire Police's dedicated web pages.

metadata.title: Reform councillor complains to Parliament over MP’s response to 199-home plan
metadata.contentSnippet: A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Reform councillor complains to Parliament over MP’s response to 199-home plan
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury. Cllr Karan Maheshwari, who represents Ramsey on Huntingdonshire District Council, has submitted a complaint to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. It concerns North West Cambridgeshire MP Mr Carling’s response to Cllr Maheshwari’s request for him to intervene in planning application 25/01382/OUT, for 199 homes between Ramsey and Bury. A copy seen by this publication is dated November 2 and marked “DRAFT – NOT SUBMITTED”, but Cllr Maheshwari later confirmed he submitted it on November 3 and received confirmation on November 4. The dispute began after Huntingdonshire District Council’s development management committee said it was minded to reject the scheme. Cllr Maheshwari says he asked Mr Carling to urge the Secretary of State not to “call in” the application. A planning application being called in means the Government takes responsibility for deciding it instead of leaving the final decision with the local authority. Mr Carling replied in social media posts included with the complaint: “Karan, this is misinformation. MPs have no power over planning.” Mr Carling also said intervention with the Secretary of State could trigger a judicial review and give the council another route to overturn its refusal. Cllr Maheshwari disputes the suggestion that his request amounted to misinformation. He argues that, although an MP cannot decide a planning application, an MP can make representations about a planning case. The row continued the next day when Cllr Maheshwari posted a further criticism of Mr Carling and urged him to stand up for residents. The councillor accepts in his complaint that the post contained “direct political criticism”, including a call for Mr Carling to stand down if he would not represent residents’ concerns. Mr Carling replied that there was “absolutely no need for full-on personal nastiness” and said voters wanted politicians to work together. He added: “I am not going to engage. Particularly when most of what you're doing is AI-generated anyway.” The AI reference forms another part of Cllr Maheshwari’s complaint. The Reform councillor argues that using AI to research or draft material should not by itself discredit someone’s arguments. He stresses that he is not accusing Mr Carling of unlawful discrimination and accepts that the comments do not prove a wider policy of refusing to engage with AI users. Instead, Cllr Maheshwari asks whether residents’ or elected representatives’ concerns could be dismissed because they used AI to prepare their arguments. The complaint asks the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards to consider whether the exchanges breached Rule 11 of the House of Commons Code of Conduct. Rule 11 covers conduct serious enough to damage the reputation and integrity of the House of Commons or MPs generally. Cllr Maheshwari accepts that the rule sets a high bar and that an ordinary political disagreement would not normally be enough. The complaint acknowledges that the Commissioner may decide the matter is not serious enough to investigate. If that happens, Cllr Maheshwari has asked the Commissioner to consider whether the concerns should instead be raised with Mr Carling under a separate parliamentary procedure, without a formal investigation. He says the complaint is not intended to stop robust political debate or force Mr Carling to support a particular planning position. Instead, it asks for scrutiny of how elected representatives handle public concerns. The document includes screenshots of the exchanges and copies of Cllr Maheshwari’s posts as evidence. A Facebook post at the centre of the dispute has since been removed, but Cllr Maheshwari says he does not know who deleted it or why and makes no allegation about its removal. Mr Carling has been approached for comment. The application was submitted by David Wilson Homes South Midlands.

Rare Royal Mint 50p coin sells for more than 420 times face value on eBay
metadata.contentSnippet: Only 210,000 of the 2009 Kew Gardens 50p coins entered circulation.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Rare Royal Mint 50p coin sells for more than 420 times face value on eBay
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A rare 50p coin has fetched more than 400 times its face value after an online auction. The 2009 Kew Gardens piece drew 19 bids on eBay on November 4. A winning bid of £221.36 landed the coin, with an extra £9.55 buyer protection fee included. Released by the Royal Mint in 2009, the Kew Gardens 50p had a circulating mintage of 210,000. It marks the 250th anniversary of the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew. Its reverse shows the Great Pagoda encircled by a climbing vine, while the obverse carries a portrait of Queen Elizabeth II. The Royal Mint ranks the 2009 Kew Gardens coin as the second-rarest 50p to enter circulation by mintage, behind the 2023 Atlantic Salmon. It says demand for the 50p denomination was low in 2009, accounting for the unusually small number struck that year. The 50p piece has a seven-sided shape and provides space for commemorative designs. The Kew Gardens 50p measures 27.30mm across. A coin's mintage, design and condition can all influence its value, according to the Royal Mint. An unusually low mintage may mean a coin sells for more than face value on the secondary market. Condition can also matter, with coins closer to mint condition potentially worth more. The Royal Mint advises collectors to research secondary-market listings and consult a coin expert if in doubt. The price paid for this graded Kew Gardens coin does not guarantee the same return for another example. Royal Mint figures list these 50p coins among the rarest to enter circulation, ranked by mintage: The 2023 Atlantic Salmon coin has the lowest mintage of any 50p issued for circulation, according to the Royal Mint. Collectors can check the Royal Mint's published mintage figures to find out how many examples of a circulating design were issued.

metadata.title: Thousands of Vauxhall owners warned 'stop driving' over safety issue
metadata.contentSnippet: Check which Vauxhall models are affected by the Takata airbag recall, how the stop-drive advice works and how to book a free repair.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Thousands of Vauxhall owners warned 'stop driving' over safety issue
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Thousands of Vauxhall drivers have been told to stop driving over an airbag safety risk. Stellantis UK, Vauxhall's parent company, issued the stop-drive instruction for certain vehicles fitted with Takata airbags, which were already part of a recall. Vauxhall says the airbag inflator can degrade over time in high heat and humidity and may explode with excessive force in a crash, causing serious injury or death. Law firm Bond Turner estimates the recall affects 320,000 vehicles and is investigating potential claims over motorists' losses. The firm's estimate is not a confirmed count of vehicles currently subject to the stop-drive instruction. Vauxhall says drivers who receive a stop-drive warning should stop using the vehicle as soon as it is safe to do so. Its recall page lists the following models under the stop-drive action: Astra Hatch (2005 to 2015), Astra Van (2006 to 2013), Astra Twin Top (2006 to 2015), Vectra (2005 to 2008) and Signum (2005 to 2008). Not every vehicle in those model ranges is necessarily affected, and owners should check their vehicle identification number (VIN) to see whether their car is included and what action is advised. Vauxhall says the only exception to the stop-drive instruction is a direct journey, without stops, to a pre-booked recall repair appointment, provided the vehicle can be driven there lawfully. Other models are subject to the recall but not the stop-drive instruction, and their owners should still take action as soon as possible. These are the Astra J and Astra GTC (2010 to 2018), Meriva B (2010 to 2017), Mokka and Mokka X (2013 to 2018), Cascada (2013 to 2018) and Zafira C (2012 to 2016). Drivers can use Vauxhall's vehicle recall checker to check their VIN and register for a free repair. The 17-character VIN can be found on a V5C registration certificate or in the vehicle. Owners who cannot register online can call Vauxhall's recall helpline on 0800 917 9285. Vauxhall says registered keepers of affected vehicles will be sent a letter and should make sure their contact details are up to date with the DVLA. Bond Turner is looking into whether motorists may be able to recover expenses linked to the recall, including alternative transport, replacement vehicle hire and loss of earnings. Malcolm Lewis, head of group litigation at Bond Turner, said: "For many people, their car is essential to everyday life, whether that is getting to work, taking children to school or fulfilling family and personal commitments." Mr Lewis said: "Our investigations will look at who may be legally responsible for the losses experienced by affected motorists, including the cost of alternative transport and replacement vehicle hire, loss of earnings and other associated expenses." Vauxhall says it has made mobility solutions available for customers affected by the stop-drive action and asks them to discuss any specific needs with their retailer when booking.

metadata.title: Nationwide savers set for a welcome boost from December – how much will you get?
metadata.contentSnippet: Nationwide is raising rates on most variable savings accounts, with some paying 3.55%. It comes as bank switching jumps 55%.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Nationwide savers set for a welcome boost from December – how much will you get?
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Nationwide is increasing interest rates on the vast majority of its variable savings accounts after the Bank of England raised borrowing costs – giving savers a potential boost from next month. The building society will increase rates by up to 0.25 percentage points from December 1, with some accounts now paying 3.55%. The move follows Thursday's Bank of England decision to raise the base rate from 3.75% to 4% for the first time in more than three years. It comes as new figures show more than one million people have switched current accounts so far this year, with completed moves jumping by 55% in the third quarter compared with the same period in 2025. Nationwide was also among the biggest winners for customer switches in the second quarter, recording a net gain of 23,636 accounts. Nationwide said it was increasing rates across most of its variable-rate savings accounts from December 1. Among the changes, its 1 Year Triple Access Saver and 1 Year Triple Access ISA will both pay 3.55%, up from 3.30%. Members with a Reward Single Access ISA will see their rate increase from 2.80% to 3.05%, while Reward Saver and Reward ISA rates will rise from 2.75% to 3%. Other changes include: Rates on some instant-access accounts will also increase by up to 0.15 percentage points. Nationwide members signed up to its SavingsWatch service will be notified of changes affecting their accounts on December 1. Pella Frost, Nationwide's director of Everyday Banking, said: “Supporting our savers is important to us, which is why we have carefully reviewed our range and are increasing rates on the vast majority of our variable rate savings accounts following the Bank Rate change. “We regularly review our rates, taking account of the wider market and the value we offer. These changes follow recent increases to our fixed rate products and the launch of our market-leading Member Exclusive Bond. “We’d encourage customers to speak to us about our full range of savings products, whether in branch, online or over the phone, so that we can help them find the right account for their needs.” UK interest rates (Image: PA Wire) Virgin Money, which is part of the Nationwide group, is also increasing rates on its off-sale variable savings accounts by up to 0.25 percentage points from December 1. Its M Plus Saver rate will rise from 1.75% to 2% on balances up to £25,000, while the rate on balances above that amount will increase from 1.25% to 1.50%. The savings announcement comes as figures from the Current Account Switch Service (Cass) reveal that 411,384 current account switches were completed between July and September 2026. That was up 55% on the 265,083 recorded during the same quarter last year, and the highest quarterly total since the final three months of 2023. September was the busiest month, with 152,299 switches completed. The latest figures take the total number of completed switches in 2026 to 1,019,912. Nationwide was among the biggest beneficiaries in the second quarter, recording a net gain of 23,636 customers switching to it. It was followed by Barclays, with a net gain of 21,169, NatWest with 20,287 and Monzo with 17,544. Do you understand ISAs? They’re changing: cash, shares, LISAs and more, what you need to know and do now! Plus State Pension tax help, mortgage rate rises & more. All in the new Martin Lewis podcast... https://t.co/O7b14FLwb2 https://t.co/RCrSyznDx9 And elsewhere... — Martin Lewis (@MartinSLewis) November 5, 2026 Other providers saw more customers leave than join. Halifax recorded a net loss of 20,728 switches, while TSB lost 17,008 and Santander lost 14,124. The figures are based on information voluntarily provided by banks and building societies and cover switches made through Cass, rather than every account move. Fred Powell, head of current accounts at Nationwide, highlighted the society's “fairer share” payments to members, its promise to keep branches open until at least the start of 2030 and services including dementia clinics. Abigail Foster, a personal finance expert at Compare the Market, said: “With over one million switches completed so far in 2026, it’s encouraging to see so many people exploring their options. “With continued pressure on household budgets, ensuring that your money is working as hard as possible is essential. “Switching accounts could potentially provide better interest rates, lower fees, and enhanced benefits.” John Dentry, product manager at Pay.UK, which owns and operates Cass, said: “The huge range of providers underscores the competitiveness of the market.” The Current Account Switch Service is designed to make moving banks or building societies easier. Payments going into and out of an old account are automatically transferred to the new one, and a guarantee is in place to protect customers if something goes wrong with the switch. Customers can also move their current account outside the scheme if they prefer. Small businesses with a turnover of up to £6.5million, small charities with an annual income below £6.5million and small trusts with net assets below £6.5million can also use the service. Smaller banks are also trying to tempt customers to switch by offering perks and rewards on their current accounts. Zopa, for example, has revamped its Biscuit current account to let customers choose the benefits that best suit their spending habits. The free account pays 1% AER variable interest on all balances and offers fee-free card spending abroad, while customers can select one additional benefit: 2.75% AER variable interest on their balance, 3% cashback on up to £150 of eating-out spending each month, or 3% cashback on up to £150 of Direct Debit payments each month. Recommended reading: The latest available figures for net completed switches between April and June show how providers fared among customers using Cass. The figures show net gains or losses through the switching service only and do not include customers who moved accounts outside Cass.

metadata.title: DWP confirms State Pension age change - people with these birthdays face longer wait
metadata.contentSnippet: People approaching State Pension age are being warned they could have to wait several months longer before receiving their first payment as the Government continues its phased increase from 66 to 67.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP confirms State Pension age change - people with these birthdays face longer wait
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: People approaching State Pension age are being warned they could have to wait several months longer before receiving their first payment as the Government continues its phased increase from 66 to 67. The change is being introduced gradually over two years, with the State Pension age rising by one month at a time for people reaching 66 during the transition. The next stage begins on November 6 and affects people born between November 6 and December 5, 1960. Rather than receiving their State Pension when they turn 66, this group will have to wait until they are 66 years and eight months old before becoming eligible. For someone born on November 6, 1960, that means they will reach State Pension age on July 6, 2027. The delay increases by another month for each subsequent group of birthdays. Those born between December 6, 1960 and January 5, 1961 will have to wait until they are 66 years and nine months old, while the next group will reach State Pension age at 66 years and 10 months. The phased increase will eventually mean people born from March 6, 1961 onwards have to wait until their 67th birthday to claim their State Pension. The State Pension age is currently 66 for men and women, but is rising to 67 between 2026 and 2028. The increase began on April 6, 2026, and affects people born between April 6, 1960 and April 5, 1961. The exact age at which someone can claim depends on their date of birth, with the delay increasing by one month for each successive group. The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) timetable is: The latest increase comes amid calls for the State Pension age to be reduced to 65 for everyone. A public petition calling for the change has attracted thousands of signatures, with campaigners arguing that people in their mid-to-late 60s can face poor health, caring responsibilities and limited options to remain in work. Tim Grimsditch, Managing Director of Unbiased, said: “A public petition calling for the State Pension age to be reduced to 65 for everyone has gathered more than 80,000 signatures and is approaching the 100,000 needed for Parliament to consider debating it. Its argument is that many people aged 65 to 67 face poor health, caring pressures, and limited options to keep working - and the evidence that healthy life expectancy varies considerably by income and occupation gives that weight. “The Government has consistently rejected calls to lower the State Pension age, and the Third State Pension Age Review is currently underway to determine what the age should be in future decades. There’s a difficult balance here: the State Pension is one of the largest items of public spending, and allowing people to claim it earlier would mean paying it to more people for longer. Both sides of this are serious arguments. “Either way, the timing matters for planning. The State Pension age is currently rising from 66 to 67, a change that began in April 2026 and completes in March 2028, affecting people born between March 1961 and August 1977. Legislation already exists to take it to 68 after that. “The practical issue for most people isn’t the State Pension age itself - it’s the gap before it. "Private pensions can generally be accessed from 55, rising to 57 in April 2028, while the State Pension now arrives at 67. Someone who stops working at 63 through ill health or caring responsibilities is funding four years entirely from their own provision. That’s the question the petition is really about, and it’s worth planning for regardless of what happens to it." Recommended reading: The increase from 66 to 67 was brought forward under the Pensions Act 2014. The legislation changed the timetable so that the State Pension age for men and women would rise to 67 between 2026 and 2028, rather than over the longer period previously planned. The DWP said: “The Pensions Act 2014 brought the increase in the State Pension age from 66 to 67 forward by eight years. The State Pension age for men and women will now increase to 67 between 2026 and 2028. “The Government also changed the way in which the increase in State Pension age is phased so that rather than reaching State Pension age on a specific date, people born between 6 April 1960 and 5 March 1961 will reach their State Pension age at 66 years and the specified number of months. “For people born after 5 April 1969 but before 6 April 1977, under the Pensions Act 2007, State Pension age was already 67.”

metadata.title: Walkers crisps and Rubicon drink recalled from UK supermarket shelves
metadata.contentSnippet: Check affected Rubicon drink and Walkers snack box batches, allergy risks and refund advice from the Food Standards Agency.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Walkers crisps and Rubicon drink recalled from UK supermarket shelves
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A drink and a snack box feature in this week's round-up of product recalls. AG Barr is recalling Rubicon Yuzu & Pink Grapefruit cartons, while PepsiCo is recalling its Walkers Variety Snacks Sharing Box. The Food Standards Agency (FSA) has published allergy alerts for both products, including details of which batches are affected and what customers should do. The FSA says the 1L cartons may contain sulphites not mentioned on the label, posing a possible health risk to people sensitive to sulphur dioxide or sulphites. Four batches are affected: Anyone with a sensitivity to sulphur dioxide or sulphites who has bought an affected carton should not consume it, the FSA advises. They can return it to the shop where it was bought for a full refund, or contact consumercare@agbarr.co.uk for further information. The FSA says notices explaining the recall will be displayed in retail stores selling the product. PepsiCo is recalling the 655g box of six packs because wheat is not declared on the outer packaging, according to the FSA. The problem concerns an 85g pack of Monster Munch Giants Roast Beef inside the box, which contains wheat and gluten. The affected batch code is 107543, with best-before dates of 21 November 2026 or 16 January 2027. The FSA says the product poses a possible health risk to people with an allergy or intolerance to wheat or gluten, or with coeliac disease. Those customers are advised not to eat the affected product and can contact the PepsiCo Consumer Care Line on 0800274777 or visit contact.pepsico.com/walkers for a full refund. The alert applies to England, Scotland and Wales. The FSA explains that a food may be withdrawn from sale when there is a problem that means it should not be sold. A recall is when customers are asked to return the product, rather than it simply being taken off shelves. Food can be withdrawn or recalled because allergy information is missing or incorrect, or because there is another food allergy risk. When there is a food allergy risk, the agency issues an allergy alert.

You can see the full methodology and learn more about how Downdetector collects status information and detects problems via its website. metadata.title: WATCH: Drunk e-scooter rider banned from driving after crash
metadata.contentSnippet: A man has been banned from driving after riding a rental e-scooter while drunk in Cambridge.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: WATCH: Drunk e-scooter rider banned from driving after crash
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been banned from driving after riding a rental e-scooter while drunk. CCTV showed Neil McGovern, 43, staggering along Cambridge’s St Andrew’s Street shortly after midnight on June 21 before riding away on an e-scooter. About 10 minutes later, ambulance crews alerted police after finding a man unconscious with a serious head injury following an e-scooter crash. McGovern, of River Lane, Cambridge, was taken to Addenbrooke’s Hospital for treatment, where a blood sample revealed he had 204 milligrams of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood—more than twice the legal limit of 80 milligrams. After recovering, he attended a voluntary police interview but gave no comment when shown CCTV footage of himself riding the e-scooter. He pleaded guilty to drink driving and was disqualified from driving for 20 months at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on November 5. PC Jack Brown said: "Some people may not realise that e-scooters are classed as motor vehicles and the same drink driving laws apply as they do to cars." McGovern was also ordered to pay more than £1,000 in fines and costs. Private e-scooters remain banned on UK public roads and pavements, although authorised rental schemes operate in trial areas.

metadata.title: 'A sad loss': Hunts residents react to beloved department store closing
metadata.contentSnippet: Beloved department store chain Townrow has announced it will be closing its St Ives store, sparking sadness among residents.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'A sad loss': Hunts residents react to beloved department store closing
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A beloved Huntingdonshire department store has announced it will be closing, sparking sadness among residents. Family-run department store Townrow, which opened in 1871, said it had not taken the “difficult” decision to close its St Ives store lightly. The independent chain sells clothing, shoes and kitchenware, with stores in Maldon and Frinton-on-Sea, Essex. Managing Director Edward Townrow said: "Like many independent retailers, we have faced increasingly challenging trading conditions, rising operating costs and changes in shopping habits. "Despite exploring a number of alternatives, we have regrettably been unable to establish a financially sustainable future for the store in its current form." Residents were asked to share their thoughts on the closure. Judith Brass said: "It's a sad loss for the town. "It's pretty much the only place worth shopping at for ladies. "We have such great eating places in St Ives nowadays, I was hoping the town was on the up so this is a blow." Ms Natalie Flack praised Townrow for stocking “concession brands like Vera Moda, Mango, Radley, Barbour” and said the staff are wonderful. She added: "I hope they get given another chance." Anne Dellar said: “Personally I am very sorry to see Townrow closing...this will be an enormous loss to St Ives. "More importantly my thoughts are with the staff of Townrow and sincerely hope that other local businesses who may be looking for staff can contact the Townrow staff for vacancies they may be looking to fill before looking further afield." Diane Langley said: "It's sad. The store had character unlike the national chains." However, other residents said they hoped popular chains such as M&S Food took over the premises. Miriam Rogers said: "Maybe we could have a Home Bargains in that space for St Ives." Alison Smith added: "B&M or Home Bargains would be good in its place." The store will hold a closing-down sale in the coming weeks.

metadata.title: Convicted sex offender jailed after creating secret social media account
metadata.contentSnippet: A convicted sex offender from Great Shelford, Cambridgeshire, has been jailed for breaching a court order after creating a secret social media account on Kik.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Convicted sex offender jailed after creating secret social media account
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A convicted Cambridgeshire sex offender has been jailed for breaching a court order after creating a secret social media account. Harry Yeardsley, 20, admitted two breaches of a Sexual Harm Prevention Order (SHPO). The order was imposed earlier this year after Yeardsley pleaded guilty to sexual communication with a child. Specialist officers from the Management of Sexual Offenders and Violent Offenders (MOSOVO) unit visited Yeardsley’s home in Wheelers, Great Shelford, on November 5 as part of routine checks. During the visit, officers discovered that Yeardsley had created, used, and deleted an account on Kik, an anonymous messaging app, earlier that week, in direct violation of his SHPO. Yeardsley was arrested and later admitted two SHPO breaches. He was jailed for six months at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on Friday, November 6. Detective Sergeant Andy Harding said: "Sexual harm prevention orders are there to manage risk and safeguard the public. "Breaching them is a serious offence, and we will take robust action against anyone who fails to comply. "I would encourage anyone with concerns about someone’s behaviour, particularly where children may be at risk, to report it to us."

metadata.title: Romesh Ranganathan tackles online outrage and family life in sharp Cambs comedy show
metadata.contentSnippet: Romesh Ranganathan brings his sell-out Will Change Your Life tour to Cambridge, tackling family, racism and online outrage with sharp, self-deprecating comedy.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Romesh Ranganathan tackles online outrage and family life in sharp Cambs comedy show
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridge welcomed Romesh Ranganathan as part of his sell-out 'Romesh Will Change Your Life' tour, with the evening proving to be anything but a conventional comedy show. A live DJ, a sell-out audience and a comedian with absolutely no intention of playing it safe, the TV star delivered an evening of sharp wit, awkward truths and wonderfully self-deprecating humour. Before the, a live DJ set was accompanied by various clips from Romesh's television appearances, including Rob & Romesh and his recent winning moment on Celebrity Traitors. It was an unconventional opening, but one that immediately established the atmosphere of the evening. From family life and relationships to racism, immigration and wider social issues, no subject was entirely off limits. Romesh moved effortlessly between everyday observations and contentious topics, delivering his trademark dry humour with a healthy dose of self-deprecation. Romesh Ranganathan on the Cambridge Corn Exchange stage (Image: Angela Smith) He also addressed the recent controversy surrounding his BBC TV advert "What has the BBC ever done for me", which attracted online criticism and abuse directed at both him and his wife. Rather than shy away from the subject, he used it as another opportunity to expose the absurdities of online outrage and the world of keyboard warriors. However, some of the evening's biggest laughs came when Romesh turned his attention closer to home. Joking about being fed up with seeing himself on television, he launched into imagined stand-up performances by his wife and son. His ability to impersonate his own family, while simultaneously making himself the butt of the joke, proved a particular highlight, generating some of the most raucous laughter of the night. He weaved jokes about his childhood trauma and his womanising dad into a therapy-themed narrative, which made it feel as though he was baring his soul on stage under the guise of comedy. It is this willingness to ridicule himself, alongside his sharp observations and unapologetic approach to difficult subjects, that makes Romesh such an engaging performer. 'Will Change Your Life' may be a bold promise, but if the measure is an evening of laughter, uncomfortable truths and refreshingly honest humour, Cambridge certainly got its money's worth.

metadata.title: Motorist helps police stop swerving lorry on A1
metadata.contentSnippet: A concerned member of the public went out of their way to help keep other motorists safe after spotting a lorry swerving across the M11.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Motorist helps police stop swerving lorry on A1
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A quick-thinking member of the public helped prevent a potential tragedy on the roads. They raised the alarm after spotting a lorry swerving dangerously across the M11 on November 2. The caller, who continued to follow the vehicle and used their hazard lights to warn other drivers, described the lorry veering across lanes, drifting onto the hard shoulder, and nearly colliding with several vehicles. Police intercepted the lorry and used “follow me” signs to guide it safely off the A1 at Brampton Hut Services. Driver George Nadejde, 35, of Byron Road, Harrow, failed a roadside breath test with a reading of 112 microgrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath—more than three times the legal limit of 35. A later evidential reading in custody showed 102 microgrammes. Nadejde pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and drink-driving at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on November 3. He was handed a 24-week jail sentence, suspended for a year, and banned from driving for two years. PC James Westlake, from the Road Policing Unit, said: "We would like to thank the member of the public who called us, recognised the danger this driver potentially posed and went out of their way to help keep other road users safe until we could get there. "Driving a vehicle of this size while over the alcohol limit could have had devastating consequences."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire is set to be swamped in thick fog after a yellow weather warning was issued. The Met Office has put a warning in place from 6pm today (November 8) until 11am tomorrow which stretches from the south coast as far as York and from the east coast to much of Wales. "Fog patches will form readily again during Sunday evening and overnight becoming extensive by Monday morning," the warning reads. "Some dense patches of fog are expected with visibility down to around 50 metres or less in some places. Fog thinning slowly later on Monday morning." The Met Office is warning that the fog could bring travel delays, adding: "Give yourself the best chance of avoiding delays by checking road conditions if driving, leaving extra journey time, or amending plans if necessary. "Make sure you know how to switch on your fog lights, and check they are working before setting off on your journey. "Bus and train services, as well as flights and ferry travel may also be affected. Check for updates from your travel company and follow their advice. "Be prepared for weather warnings to change. When a weather warning is issued, the Met Office recommends staying up to date with the weather forecast in your area." The Met Office has classed the warning as high likelihood and a moderate impact.

metadata.title: 1,700 Cambridgeshire households urged to claim unclaimed Healthy Start support
metadata.contentSnippet: Families in Cambridgeshire are being encouraged to apply for the NHS Healthy Start scheme through a new outreach campaign.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 1,700 Cambridgeshire households urged to claim unclaimed Healthy Start support
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Families in Cambridgeshire are being encouraged to apply for the NHS Healthy Start scheme through a new outreach campaign. Cambridgeshire County Council, in partnership with district and city councils, is targeting around 1,700 low-income households identified via its Low-Income Family Tracker (LIFT) platform. The campaign will run throughout November and aims to raise awareness of unclaimed financial support for healthy food and milk. Councillor Alison Whelan, chair of the Communities, Social Mobility and Inclusion Committee, said: "We know that many families across Cambridgeshire continue to face significant cost-of-living pressures, and Healthy Start can provide valuable support at a time when every pound counts. "Through this targeted campaign, we're helping families access money that they are entitled to, putting additional income into household budgets while supporting healthy eating and giving children the best possible start in life." Healthy Start is a national scheme offering pregnant women and families with young children weekly payments of £4.65 per child under the age of four, rising to £9.30 for infants under one. The funds are loaded onto a payment card and can be used in most supermarkets to buy items such as cow’s milk, fresh fruit, and vegetables. The campaign is part of the council’s wider anti-poverty programme, which includes income maximisation services, targeted outreach, and crisis payments. Just 62 per cent of eligible Cambridgeshire families currently claim Healthy Start, meaning more than £431,000 could be going unclaimed each year. Households that have been identified will be contacted by letter, email, phone call, or text message. Those who do not receive a notification are still encouraged to check their eligibility through the NHS Healthy Start website. Residents are reminded that if they are ever in doubt about the authenticity of a letter, email, text message or phone call, they can contact their district or city council directly for verification. Information on scam awareness is available on the Cambridgeshire County Council website.
